reason: Section 190.04 is a remedial power: after non-compliance with a confirmed notice, the municipality may do the work, enter to do it, charge the cost as a debt, and avoid compensation liability when acting reasonably.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal cleanup, repair, demolition, entry, debt, and immunity
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.04 is a remedial power: after non-compliance with a confirmed notice, the municipality may do the work, enter to do it, charge the cost as a debt, and avoid compensation liability when acting reasonably.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a municipality may clean up, repair or demolish dangerous or unsightly premises and how entry, debt and compensation immunity work.

reason: Section 190.041 separates emergency notice and immediate municipal action from cost recovery, liability protection, and post-action statements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Emergency notice and immediate action to terminate danger
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections define emergency, authorize an officer to prepare an immediate-work notice after inspection, and permit measures to terminate the danger before or after notice is given.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an emergency dangerous-premises notice may be prepared and when municipal entry and measures may occur to terminate danger.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Emergency work liability, debt, and post-measure notice statements
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections protect reasonable municipal action from compensation liability, make emergency measure costs a debt, and require copies of the notice or statement after measures are taken.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the liability, cost-debt, and follow-up notice rules after emergency dangerous-premises measures are taken.

reason: Section 190.042 prohibits refusing entry to or obstructing an officer exercising entry powers and sets category F offence, special leased-dwelling minimum fine, and continuing-offence fine rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Obstruction of municipal entry and continuing penalties
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.042 prohibits refusing entry to or obstructing an officer exercising entry powers and sets category F offence, special leased-dwelling minimum fine, and continuing-offence fine rules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the offence and fine rules for obstructing an officer or municipal agent entering to carry out dangerous-premises work.

reason: Section 190.05 lets a municipal officer certify the work-measure debt, file it in court, enforce it as a judgment, and recover filing and recording costs.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Certificate enforcement of dangerous-premises work debts
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.05 lets a municipal officer certify the work-measure debt, file it in court, enforce it as a judgment, and recover filing and recording costs.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how a municipality can convert dangerous-premises work costs into a court-enforceable judgment debt.

reason: Section 190.06 creates and describes the priority lien for cleanup, repair, demolition or emergency measure costs and allows secured creditors to pay the lien and add it to their security.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Priority lien for dangerous-premises work costs
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.06 creates and describes the priority lien for cleanup, repair, demolition or emergency measure costs and allows secured creditors to pay the lien and add it to their security.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when dangerous-premises work costs form a lien, how the lien attaches and follows the property, and what secured claimants may do.

reason: Section 190.061 has separate topics for provincial payment to the municipality, provincial tax-style recovery from owners, and the resulting lien or proceeds charge.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister of Finance payment to municipality for unpaid dangerous-premises debt
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 190.061(1) and (2) state when the Minister of Finance pays the municipality unpaid debt and interest and how the municipality requests payment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the conditions, timing, interest, and statement requirement for provincial payment of unpaid dangerous-premises debts to a municipality.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Provincial recovery of dangerous-premises debt through real property tax collection
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 190.061(3) and (4) make the unpaid amount a debt to the Minister of Finance and apply specified Real Property Tax Act provisions with modifications for collection.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how unpaid dangerous-premises debt shifts to the Minister of Finance and is collected from the owner through tax-collection rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Lien and proceeds charge for amounts collected by the Minister of Finance
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 190.061(5) and (6) address the lien on real property and charge on sale proceeds when the recovered amounts remain unpaid.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the lien ranking and proceeds-charge rules for unpaid amounts collected by the Minister of Finance.

reason: Section 190.07 requires a report from an architect, engineer, building inspector or Fire Marshal before the municipality acts under paragraph 190.04(1)(b), and gives that report evidentiary effect.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Expert report prerequisite for municipal demolition

evidenceText: proof in the absence of evidence

proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.07 requires a report from an architect, engineer, building inspector or Fire Marshal before the municipality acts under paragraph 190.04(1)(b), and gives that report evidentiary effect.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what report is required before municipal demolition for a dangerous structure and what the report proves.

reason: Section 190.0705 defines service for sections 190.071 to 190.09 as a service prescribed by regulation unless context requires otherwise.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Service definition for rural community provisions

evidenceText: service means, unless the context requires otherwise

proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.0705 defines service for sections 190.071 to 190.09 as a service prescribed by regulation unless context requires otherwise.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the meaning of service in the rural community provisions.

reason: Section 190.071 authorizes regulations setting conditions, procedures and criteria before incorporation or boundary changes, requires or permits dissolution feasibility studies, and reserves dissolution to a special Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulatory prerequisites, feasibility study, and special-Act dissolution for rural communities
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.071 authorizes regulations setting conditions, procedures and criteria before incorporation or boundary changes, requires or permits dissolution feasibility studies, and reserves dissolution to a special Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the prerequisite regulation subjects, dissolution study trigger, and special-Act rule for rural communities.

reason: Section 190.072 sets the regulation-making authority for rural community incorporation, amalgamation, annexation and decrement, and includes a contiguity rule for groups of annexed areas.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations incorporating, amalgamating, annexing, or decreasing rural communities
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.072 sets the regulation-making authority for rural community incorporation, amalgamation, annexation and decrement, and includes a contiguity rule for groups of annexed areas.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulatory actions available for rural community boundaries and how grouped contiguous annexations are treated.
